specs.anchorText: five families of transformations, each one a strict superset of the one before
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins: a friendly cartoon smartphone character with a cheerful face holding a small magic wand, pointing at a crumpled receipt that is photographed as a tilted lopsided trapezoid floating in the air; a gentle glowing arc shows the trapezoid being gently straightened into a crisp neat upright rectangle that looks like a clean scanned page. Soft blues and warm yellows, expressive and gentle, like an XKCD-inspired infographic meets Kurzgesagt. The composition is simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor: a wonky photo becoming a tidy scan through geometry. No text or lettering in the image. Tasteful and inclusive, gentle humor.
specs.alt: A friendly cartoon smartphone waves a small wand at a tilted trapezoidal photo of a crumpled receipt, and a glowing arc straightens it into a crisp upright rectangle resembling a clean flatbed scan, illustrating how a small matrix and a resampling step turn a wonky angled snapshot into a flat document.
specs.caption: Every phone scanner is the same trick: a little matrix tells each pixel where to go, and interpolation decides what color it carries when it lands.

specs.anchorText: each one trading away an invariant in exchange for expressive power
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a five-rung ladder climbing upward to the right, with five friendly cartoon square-shaped characters standing one per rung, each slightly more distorted than the last. The bottom square is a perfect upright square holding tightly to its shape; the next is the same square but rotated; the next is rotated and shrunk; the next is sheared into a leaning parallelogram looking a bit loose; the top one is stretched into a perspective trapezoid as if seen vanishing into the distance, looking dramatic. Each character cheerfully drops a little token as it climbs (a tiny ruler, a compass, a pair of parallel rails) to suggest giving up one property per step. Soft pastel blues, greens, and oranges, expressive faces. No text or lettering in the image. One clear visual metaphor: climbing the ladder means surrendering one invariant at a time. Gentle and inclusive humor.
specs.alt: Five friendly square characters climb a five-rung ladder, each more distorted than the one below: a perfect square, then rotated, then scaled, then sheared into a parallelogram, then stretched into a perspective trapezoid, each dropping a small token like a ruler or a pair of rails to show one geometric invariant being surrendered at every rung.
specs.caption: Climb the hierarchy and you trade away one invariant per rung: position, then orientation, then scale, then angles, then parallelism, until only straightness survives at the top.

specs.anchorText: Represent the 2D point $(x, y)$ as the 3-vector $(x, y, 1)$
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a friendly cartoon point character (a small round dot with a happy face and little legs) wearing a tiny backpack labeled only with a small number-like badge shaped like the digit one (no other text). The point is happily walking from one spot to another along a flat grid floor, and the act of walking (a translation) is drawn as gliding smoothly along a clean straight track, suggesting that carrying the extra item turned an awkward move into a simple, tidy slide. Around it, a faint hint of a multiplication grid suggests linear algebra. Soft warm yellows and blues, gentle and expressive. No text or lettering in the image except the single digit-one badge shape. One focused visual metaphor: an extra coordinate in the backpack makes moving house count as plain matrix math. Inclusive, gentle humor.
specs.alt: A cheerful round point character with little legs wears a small backpack badged with the digit one and glides smoothly along a straight track across a grid floor, illustrating how appending a third coordinate of one to a 2D point turns translation from an awkward addition into a single tidy matrix multiplication.
specs.caption: Carry one extra coordinate everywhere and moving a point becomes plain matrix multiplication, so composing and undoing warps turn into multiplying and inverting matrices.

specs.anchorText: Downscaling is a different physics problem
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a friendly cartoon striped or houndstooth-patterned sweater hanging on a hanger, being shrunk by a cartoon machine into a tiny thumbnail version; the tiny version has broken out in swirly rainbow moire ripples and looks alarmed and dizzy, while a small worried cartoon character points at it. Off to the side, a calm helper character holds a gentle blur brush labeled by a small soft-cloud icon (no text) suggesting an anti-alias filter that would have prevented the problem. Soft blues, warm oranges, with a controlled splash of swirly rainbow only on the broken thumbnail. Expressive and gentle. No text or lettering in the image. One clear visual metaphor: shrinking a busy pattern without filtering first produces garish moire. Tasteful, inclusive, gentle humor.
specs.alt: A patterned sweater is shrunk by a cartoon machine into a tiny thumbnail that breaks out in dizzy swirly rainbow moire ripples while a worried character points and a calm helper holds a soft blur brush, illustrating that downscaling a high-frequency texture without an anti-alias low-pass filter folds detail back as aliasing artifacts.
specs.caption: Shrinking is sampling, and sampling without an anti-alias filter folds fine texture back as garish moire; the fix is one flag, but the bug is silent until it poisons everything downstream.

specs.anchorText: loop over the output, not the input
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a split scene contrasting two cartoon workers filling a fresh empty grid of pixel buckets. On the left, a flustered worker tosses paint blobs forward from a full input grid toward an output grid, but some output buckets are left empty (a few sad empty holes) and others get splattered twice, looking messy. On the right, a calm relaxed worker stands at the empty output grid and instead reaches a long arm back to the source image to scoop exactly the right color for each bucket, so every bucket is filled neatly with no holes. Soft greens for the calm correct method, soft reds for the messy one. Expressive characters. No text or lettering in the image. One clear visual metaphor: pulling each output pixel from the source beats pushing input pixels forward. Gentle, inclusive humor.
specs.alt: A split cartoon contrasts forward mapping, where a flustered worker tosses paint forward and leaves empty holes and double splatters in the output grid, against inverse mapping, where a calm worker stands at each empty output pixel and reaches back to the source image to scoop exactly the right value, filling every pixel once with no holes.
specs.caption: Stand at the destination and ask where each pixel came from: looping over the output and pulling from the input fills every pixel exactly once, with no holes and no collisions.

specs.anchorText: make the system indifferent to incorrect measurements
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a friendly cartoon referee character (whistle, striped shirt) standing among a crowd of little arrow-shaped voter characters. Most arrows (the inliers, drawn in calm blue) confidently point the same direction along a neat consensus lane, while a scattered minority of confused arrows (the outliers, drawn in red) point every which way. The referee cheerfully gives a thumbs-up to the agreeing blue majority and calmly waves off the scattered red ones, unbothered. A faint shaded lane shows the agreed-upon direction. Soft blues, warm neutrals, a little red for the dissenters. Expressive and gentle. No text or lettering in the image. One clear visual metaphor: a robust estimator trusts the consensus and shrugs off the wrong votes. Inclusive, gentle humor.
specs.alt: A friendly cartoon referee stands among arrow-shaped voters, giving a thumbs-up to a calm blue majority that all point the same way along a shaded consensus lane while waving off a scattered red minority pointing every which way, illustrating how RANSAC keeps the largest set of correspondences that agree on one transform and ignores the wrong matches.
specs.caption: RANSAC does not try to make every match correct; it makes the estimate indifferent to wrong ones by trusting only the largest set of correspondences that agree on a single transform.
